answer:
Run the eval with the `-j 1` flag:

```bash
promptfoo eval -j 1
```

The docs say: "However, you can run evals serially using the `-j 1` option" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]. They also say: "This serializes the eval's **target** calls: one provider and prompt at a time." [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]

Two caveats from the same page:

- Tests marked `options.runSerially` run as a separate group before the rest, so the order isn't strictly sequential even with `-j 1`: "so a config using that option does not execute in strict test-case order even at `-j 1`." [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]
- Model-graded assertions run separately. They are serialized only when grading grouping is active. If it's disabled (by a per-eval timeout or a `{{_conversation}}` variable), up to `PROMPTFOO_ASSERTIONS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` grader calls (3 by default) can overlap within a single test case [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md].

The context doesn't cover other ways to control concurrency.
